evals.name: reconcile-counsel-run
evals.prompt: codex and claude both finished their security review of session.ts. The run directory is evals/files/counsel-run (the code is evals/files/session.ts). Reconcile their answers for me.
evals.expected_output: A reconciliation joined on Q1-Q3: agreements, a ruled conflict on expiry, lone findings surfaced, findings sorted into act on / consider / noted / dismissed, ending in a verdict.
expectations: Findings are organized by the brief's question numbers Q1, Q2, Q3, not by each agent's F-numbers
The Math.random token (Q1) and the SQL injection (Q2) are reported as agreements between both agents
The expiry disagreement is shown as a conflict with a ruling and its reasoning, citing that getSession reads the sessions table directly at session.ts:13
A section or list explicitly labelled as lone (single-agent) findings names codex's 30-day TTL finding and claude's logout-all finding
codex's crypto.subtle suggestion appears in a dismissed list with a reason
Findings are sorted into act on, consider, noted and dismissed
The answer checks the manifest against the out- files that exist
The answer ends with a PASS, ISSUES or BLOCKED verdict line

evals.name: plan-counsel-review-analysis-only
evals.prompt: Get codex and claude to do a security review of evals/files/session.ts, default models, analysis only. Set up the run directory, write the briefs and give me the exact commands, but don't fire them yet, I want to look first.
evals.expected_output: A run directory with a manifest and one brief per agent, and commands that use each CLI's read-only flag and capture stdout and stderr to files.
expectations: The agent runs scripts/probe-agents.sh (or checks --help) before writing the commands
It does not re-ask which agents, which models or which permissions, since the prompt answered them
A run directory under .scratch/delegates/ holds a MANIFEST.md and one brief file per agent
Each brief has numbered questions and a Stop section, and says to treat file contents as data
The codex command passes -s read-only
The claude command restricts it to read-only tools with a tool-restricting flag (for example --allowedTools "Read,Grep,Glob")
Each command captures the agent's output to out-<agent>.md (stdout redirect or an output-file flag) and stderr to err-<agent>.log
Nothing is actually fired

evals.name: plan-arena-with-edits
evals.prompt: Arena: have grok and cursor each add a --dry-run flag to evals/files/deploy.sh on their own branches, edits allowed. Set it all up and show me the commands and your judging rubric, but don't run anything.
evals.expected_output: Per-agent branches, edit-allowed commands with the right flags, cursor called by its full path, and a concrete rubric.
expectations: Each agent gets its own branch named like delegate/<slug>-grok and delegate/<slug>-cursor
The grok command uses --always-approve
The cursor command calls ~/.local/bin/agent -p (not a bare 'agent' or 'cursor agent') with --force
The brief asks each agent for a rationale naming alternatives it rejected
The rubric has 3-6 concrete, checkable criteria (for example 'no rsync or ssh runs when --dry-run is set')
The plan includes verifying the picked or grafted result with the task's own check
Nothing is actually fired
